issues.description: Field 'numberOfTutors' has conflicting types between the problem statement UML and the solution implementation. The UML in problem_statement.md declares 'numberOfTutors: int' (line 68). In the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) the field is declared as 'private short numberOfTutors;' (line 10) and the constructor and setter use a short parameter (constructor at line 13, setter at line 58). This mismatch between the documented type (int) and the implemented field/parameters (short) can confuse students about which numeric type to use when implementing the class and its constructor/setter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of 'numberOfTutors' consistent with the UML and across the implementation. Preferred fix: change the field and related constructor/setter parameter types to int (e.g., 'private int numberOfTutors;', constructor parameter 'int numberOfTutors', and setter parameter 'int numberOfTutors'). Alternatively, if using short is intentional, update the UML in problem_statement.md to 'numberOfTutors: short' and document that choice so students and tests expect short consistently. Ensure all method signatures (constructor and setter) and the field use the same type.
